clue.text: Interrupting calm, perhaps, soft practical joke

indicators.note: the two short pieces break into the word for calm, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: a lull is a calm spell
EG, for example, stands in for 'perhaps'
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Someone describes a quiet moment broken by a gentle prank.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling someone's leg means teasing or hoaxing them, so the noun names a practical joke or hoax.

clue.text: Call the mistress, following instincts up in song

indicators.note: the reversed pair of pieces sits inside the word for a song

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or song

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the preceding pieces are read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
the id is the Freudian seat of primitive instincts

explanation.surface: A singer, guided by instinct, addresses the lady of the house in song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses F + ID to make DIF. 'Call the mistress' reads like phoning a lover, but it means to address someone as a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: To ladify is an old verb meaning to make a lady of someone or to address her as 'my lady'.

clue.text: George the First's learning a lot

parts.note: G stands for George, as in the royal cipher GR
A is first, as in A1 or the first letter
lore is accumulated knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: King George I is said to have been very well read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George the First' looks like the king, but it splits into George (G) and 'the First' (A).
explanation.definitionFit: Galore is an adverb for in abundance, plenty of something, matching 'a lot'.

clue.text: Excited, knowing particular song

parts.note: to be well up in a subject is to be knowledgeable about it
a song is an air, and a particular one is 'the' air

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled recognises a certain tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase usually means undecided, but can describe someone agitated or worked up, as in being all of a flutter.

clue.text: Left the first person in Germany one fruit tree

parts.note: ich is German for I, the first-person pronoun
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A traveller left Germany with a single fruit tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The lichi, or lychee, is a Chinese tree grown for its sweet white-fleshed fruit.

clue.text: Last of the farm animals saw, pointed

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word 'the' is taken

parts.note: a pig and a ram are both farmyard animals
a pig and a ram are both farmyard animals

explanation.surface: Someone sees the farm animals and points them out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of 'see'; it is a noun meaning a saying, qualified by 'pointed'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty saying with a pointed twist, and a saw is a proverb or maxim.

clue.text: Following disturbance, leaves garden party without Henry; those present here never forgot

indicators.note: used in the old sense of outside: the rearranged letters surround the single letter
after being disturbed, the letters of the three words are mixed up

parts.note: H is the symbol of the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: After a disturbance, guests leave a garden party, minus Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here has its old meaning, outside, so the anagram (signalled by 'Following disturbance') surrounds the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants proverbially never forget, and legend says they go to a special place to die, so those found there were unforgetting.

clue.text: Warriors contributing little to slim pickings

indicators.note: each of the two words gives only a small part of itself, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: A few soldiers chip in to a meagre haul of food.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment or body of warriors.

clue.text: Printed information put together by defences in hearing

indicators.note: the word for defences is to be heard spoken, not written

parts.note: redoubts are small fortified defensive works

explanation.surface: Printouts are compiled by the defence team at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put together by' links the definition to the wordplay; 'hearing' looks like a court session but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Readouts are displays or printouts of data from a computer or instrument.

clue.text: King in dance promoting a firm

indicators.note: the king's letter is placed inside the altered dance word
the letter a is moved up, earlier in the word, as if given promotion

parts.note: a measure is an old word for a stately dance
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch at a ball advertises a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' moves the A of MEASURE forward to give MAESURE, and 'in' puts K inside it. 'firm' looks like a company but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To firm something up, as a verb, is to settle or secure it, much as to confirm or secure it beyond doubt.

clue.text: Indian city shop hard to get accepted

indicators.note: the shop takes in the single letter, which goes inside it

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen shop
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: In an Indian city a hard-up shopkeeper hopes to be taken on.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is the major city in northern India that contains the capital, New Delhi.

clue.text: Worthless bloke, knave inhaling drug

indicators.note: the bloke takes in the drug, so its letter goes inside him

parts.note: a chap is a bloke
E is ecstasy
the jack is the knave in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A good-for-nothing rogue takes drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective cheapjack means shoddy or of inferior quality, from the name for a hawker of cheap goods.

clue.text: Hoax here that might dawn on one?

definitions.meaning: the ... in the grid, 1 across, holds the word for a hoax
dawn's earliest glow is what breaks over someone at daybreak

explanation.walkthrough: A light is crossword jargon for an entry, so the first light is 1 across, whose answer is a hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn's earliest glimmer of daylight is called first light; the first entry of the grid is literally the first light.

clue.text: Fraudulently deposits cuts for Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool etc

indicators.note: doing something fraudulently means falsifying or cooking it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Football club bosses are accused of siphoning off deposits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' is a second definition: topside is a cut of beef. Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool are leading English football clubs, i.e. sides at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading clubs in English football are the top sides of the league.

clue.text: Question: was this medicinal once? Doctors annoy with reply

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters that follow are altered

explanation.surface: Patients wonder about old remedies while doctors irritate them with answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like a noun but is a verb meaning tampers with.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a mint once widely used in herbal medicine, though now known to be toxic.

clue.text: Direction-finding line that is over Covent Garden and missing Barking

indicators.note: in an across clue, over means turned around, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: Barking is mad, so letters are scrambled, and missing says the letters of the small word are taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A London transport line runs over Covent Garden but skips Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns IE into EI. Taking A, N, D from COVENT GARDEN leaves letters that 'Barking' rearranges as GENVECTOR. Covent Garden and Barking are both London districts.
explanation.definitionFit: In linear algebra an eigenvector is a vector whose direction is unchanged by a given transformation.

clue.text: See 5
Ran in relay, perhaps changing hands, wearing contrivance for broken bones

indicators.note: right and left are the two hands, so R is swapped for L

parts.note: a relay runner sprinted, one example of running fast

explanation.surface: A relay runner fumbles the baton handover and ends up needing bandages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' looks like passing the baton, but it swaps R (right) for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A limb that is splinted has a rigid support strapped to it to hold a fracture in place.

clue.text: Chain restricting one running up arm? If so, not the subject of a 1 across!

definitions.text: arm? If so, not the subject of a 1 across!

indicators.note: the chain encloses the reversed runner

parts.note: a fob is a watch chain

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the runner is backwards

parts.note: a miler is an athlete who runs the mile

explanation.surface: A runner climbing is held back by a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 1 across: a leg is pulled, but an arm is a front limb, not a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The forelimb of a two-legged creature is its arm, as opposed to the hindlimb, the leg.

clue.text: He's done his money and he's back for mine too, note

definitions.text: He's done his money and he's back

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', in favour of
to mine is to dig
also means too
N is a compass point, and short for note

explanation.surface: A wastrel returns home to a mine, with a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link but supplies PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: In the parable the younger son squanders his inheritance and comes home to his father's welcome.

clue.text: Cry "I'm surprised!" to be taken in by surprise!!

indicators.note: the exclamation is held inside the other word

parts.note: boo! is what you shout to startle someone
oho expresses surprise

explanation.surface: A startled person shrieks after being caught out by a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Boohoo imitates noisy sobbing, so as a verb it means to cry.

clue.text: MP's rating book, pushing boundaries

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
OTT, over the top, describes going too far

explanation.surface: A politician's book rating is controversial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like a score but is a sailor. Diane Abbott is a long-serving Labour MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Diane Abbott has been a British Member of Parliament for Hackney since 1987.

clue.text: See 12
Producer of far from welcome report, for openers

definitions.text: Producer of far from welcome report, for openers

parts.words: Producer of far from welcome report, for openers
parts.note: report means a bang, and openers are those who open post, so this is a postal device that explodes when opened

explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a written account but is the sound of an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an explosive device sent through the post, which detonates on being opened.

clue.text: Accepting one's better topless

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a better is removed

parts.note: a staker is one who bets

explanation.surface: Someone who accepts reckons a gambler is half-dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like the comparative of good but means one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A taker is one who accepts something, such as an offer or a bet.

clue.text: Bird or birds rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: auks are diving seabirds such as the guillemot

explanation.surface: A bird or a flock is taking to the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a large predatory seabird that robs other birds of their catch.

clue.text: Expert group's uncovered a consequence of lying in the Sun in 2000

parts.note: thinly covered, thin on top, can mean barely covered

indicators.note: the suntan goes inside the two thousands

parts.note: K is a thousand, so two of them make 2000

parts.words: a consequence of lying in the Sun
parts.note: lying in the sun gives you a tan

explanation.surface: A panel of experts hints at a sunbathing scandal in the year 2000.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Sun' teases the British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A think tank is a body of experts that researches and advises on policy.

clue.text: Will the actor backing intro for spies give literary class?

indicators.note: going backwards, so the actor's surname is reversed

parts.note: Will Hay was an English comedy actor of the 1930s
00 begins the codename 007, read as the letters OO

explanation.surface: A question whether an actor supporting a spy film will teach a literature class.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yahoos are the brutish human creatures in Swift's Gulliver's Travels, hence a literary class of being.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels the Yahoos are a race of degraded humans, a class of creature from literature.

clue.text: Expert fingerprintee?

definitions.meaning: dabs is slang for fingerprints, so this is a hand that has been printed

explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is a skilled practitioner; dab is also slang for a fingerprint, taken from the hand.

clue.text: This aircraft's unveiling is seen in between sides, nothing 26

indicators.note: the zero goes between the two letters for the sides

parts.note: R and L, right and left, are the two sides
O looks like zero, nothing
the answer to 26 across is a brutish person, a lout

explanation.surface: A new plane is shown off between hangars to an empty crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 refers to 26 across, a boorish creature, here LOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The rollout of a new aircraft is its first public presentation as it leaves the hangar.
